seal.statement: A failed push gate, by any path, keeps the evidence that names its failure. The acceptance runner buffers every command's output into a captured artifact inside the gate checkout (spawnSync, piped), so the change proof's per-file results never reach the terminal, and gateExactSha (scripts/checks/push-gate-corpus-worktree.js, added by d9819d43e) removes that checkout on every exit; the publisher already keeps a failed gate's receipt and first failing artifact (retainGateDiagnostics, fc6db88ee, after the 2026-08-19 incident) and the direct-push gate regressed that class. Now: gateExactSha keeps the same diagnostics, through the publisher's one retainGateDiagnostics, on every non-zero return (a failed run, a replaced injection link, a dirtied checkout) before the checkout is removed, and prints where; the run summary names the failing test files of the first failing command from its captured artifact, read line by line through the bounded reader (the runner's file-level verdict lines only, the last verdict deciding, a retried-once pass green, lab-relayed lines read), bounded with an explicit withheld count and saying 'summary line absent - list may be incomplete' instead of a count when no runner summary line was captured; the verdict stays the command's status; and the pre-push banner says what actually happens.

text: History pass. fc6db88ee (2026-08-19, 'make the push gate diagnosable') added retainGateDiagnostics to scripts/publish-head.js after three ~17-minute publish runs rediscovered what a retained receipt said; the publisher calls it in its catch (publish-head.js:1206) before removing its exact-HEAD worktree. 773ffbb52 (2026-09-02) made the publisher stream the hook live, but the acceptance runner one level down still buffers each manifest command (acceptance-proof-manifest-runner.js defaultExecute: spawnSync, piped stdio, maxBuffer 64 MB) into a captured artifact. 0d5c94316 (2026-09-02) introduced the hook banner '(per-file results stream below)', false for the postpush manifest's change-proof command since that day. d9819d43e (proof-authority-integrity, 2026-09-14) introduced gateExactSha (push-gate-corpus-worktree.js --gate): every direct push gate (main, or LAGRANGE_PUSH_PROVE_BRANCH=1) now runs in a throwaway checkout removed in finally and on signal, without the retention - the 2026-08-19 class regressed for every path except npm run publish. Before d9819d43e the direct-push hook ran in place in the pusher's checkout, so its receipt and artifacts survived there. renderRunSummary printed counts and the failing command id only. Red at seal (ec63fbb00): evidence/receipt-at-seal.json, 0/7, each red for the defect (receipt not kept on the three gate returns; summary names no file / no incompleteness line).

Sibling census (places that run a long command with captured output and then delete or overwrite the only copy). SAME MECHANISM, SAME OWNER, FIXED: (1) gateExactSha (push-gate-corpus-worktree.js) - now retains through the exported publisher retainGateDiagnostics on every non-zero return. (2) Every manifest through the acceptance runner (project-hardening-proof = test:gate, -postpush, -release-tail via run-release-proof.js, developer-smoke = test:smoke) buffers each command (spawnSync piped, maxBuffer 64 MB) and the next run rmSyncs the captured artifact before re-running it; renderRunSummary (one owner for all four) now names the first failing command's failing test files on the terminal from the capture. NOT THE SAME MECHANISM, RECORDED: (3) the publisher path (publish-head.js:1206) already retains before removing its worktree; unchanged. (4) gateMaterializedTree (--ref) streams its ratchets (stdio inherit); fine. (5) solve land's change proof (scripts/solve/commands.js runChangeProof:350-357) buffers npm test (piped, maxBuffer 64 MB, 90 min timeout) and writes it whole to stderr only after the run - nothing is deleted, but nothing streams and a >64 MB output dies ENOBUFS; owner solve, separate finding, not absorbed. (6) lab test (probe.js settleLabShares/copyLabResults) streams every machine's lines live under [machine] and copies each machine's results ledger to a fixed per-machine file that the next lab test overwrites; the terminal stream is the evidence, so not the only copy. (7) placement shards: the lab worktree is removed after the shard, but the shard's stdout (verdict lines and failing excerpts) is relayed into the controller's stream first (relayShardLines) and the results ledger via placement-results= lines; fine. (8) dt-prove.js returns output tails; the publisher's detached local corpus keeps a log per sha; fine. LATENT, RECORDED: the acceptance runner's 64 MB maxBuffer - a change proof whose stdout exceeds it is killed (ENOBUFS, signal SIGTERM); the new summary then says 'the command ended by SIGTERM - list may be incomplete' rather than a count, but the cap itself is the runner-output-bound class and is not changed here. retainGateDiagnostics picks the 'newest' report by name sort, not time; harmless in a fresh gate checkout (one acceptance run per hook) and left unchanged.

Relay shapes and the denominator (brief item 5 and item 2). Measured from the code: the change proof runs the classified runner (push-gate-change-proof.js -> run-classified-test-files.js), which runs run-test-files.js once per lane batch of at most 100 files with stdio inherit, so a change proof's stdout carries ONE '# test-files ... fail=N' line PER BATCH, not one; when placed across the lab, each lab machine's lines are relayed after the controller's own files as '[machine] <line>' (relayShardLines), and every file red there is rerun on the controller, whose new column-0 verdict decides it. A strict '^not ok <path> \(' match therefore misses lab-red files that were never rerun (over the 20-file rerun cap), and 'the final # test-files line' is only the last batch's figure. Decision: the summary reads the runner's own line shapes from one owner (TEST_FILE_LINE in run-test-files.js; probe.js's duplicate regexes now import it), strips the relay prefix through one owner (RELAYED_LINE_PREFIX, exported beside the one relayedLine producer in probe.js), decides each file by its LAST verdict line, counts a '# retried-once pass' as green, and prints the count of failing files it named; the runner's summary lines are used as the completeness signal (none captured -> 'summary line absent - list may be incomplete' and no count), together with a signal-ended command and any truncated line that may be a file verdict (a line longer than the bounded reader's 256-byte prefix; the longest test path is 115 bytes). Summing fail= across summary lines was rejected as the count: placed reruns and retried files are counted twice. The captured artifact stored stdout as one JSON string, i.e. one physical line of up to 64 MB, which no line reader can use; the artifact now stores stdoutLines/stderrLines (one JSON string per physical line, schemaVersion 2) and is read through readBoundedOutput's onLinePrefix - never JSON.parse of the document. No code reads the artifact's stdout field (grep: only humans; the publisher test fixture writes its own). Witness (c) carries a relayed lab-red, a lab-red decided green on the controller, nested 'not ok N -' TAP lines and a lookalike.

Signal path. gateExactSha's signal handlers (SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP) now release the checkout through the same releaseCheckout as finally, with the conventional 128+n status, so an interrupted gate retains whatever exists before removing the checkout. In practice: the gate runs the hook with spawnSync, which blocks the event loop, so a handler cannot run until the child returns. A terminal Ctrl-C reaches the hook's process group too; the child dies, spawnSync returns with status null, runInExactCheckout returns failure and finally retains then removes - the handler fires afterwards on an already-removed checkout (removeWorktree then is a reported no-op). A SIGTERM sent to the gate process alone waits for the hook to finish. And the acceptance runner writes its report only after its last command, so an interrupted run usually has no report and retention prints '[push-gate] no acceptance receipt to retain from the gate checkout; the output above is all the gate left' - stated, not silent.

gateExactSha split into gateExactSha + runInExactCheckout; one status flag (initialised to failure, so a throw retains too) decides in finally, and the signal handlers call the same releaseCheckout, which on any non-zero status calls the publisher's retainGateDiagnostics (now exported; no second implementation) and prints '[push-gate] gate diagnostics retained in <dir>' or that there was nothing to retain, then removes the checkout. Acceptance runner: the captured artifact stores stdoutLines/stderrLines (schemaVersion 2, one JSON string per physical line) and exports readCapturedStdout, which reads it through run-test-files' readBoundedOutput (onLinePrefix), never JSON.parse of the document. run-test-files.js owns TEST_FILE_LINE (verdict, retried-once pass, summary line shapes; probe.js's duplicate regexes now import it) and testFileVerdictReader (last verdict decides, retried pass green, summary lines counted). probe.js owns the relay shape (relayedLine producer + exported RELAYED_LINE_PREFIX). renderRunSummary(run, root) appends, for the first failing command, 'failing test files: N' (or 'summary line absent - list may be incomplete' / 'the command ended by SIGx - ...' / 'N verdict line(s) too long to read - ...' instead of N), at most 20 files, and '... W more withheld (all in <artifact>)'; verdict unchanged. Hook banner corrected (stage text + comment).
